Pretense

/PREE-tens/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Pretense means a false appearance or action intended to deceive — a pretending.

The salesman got inside dozens of homes under the pretense of offering a free safety inspection.

Worked Example

The reporter arranged a job interview at the warehouse, but the interview was a pretense — her real goal was to document the unsafe working conditions inside.

The interview looked genuine from the outside, but it was staged to conceal her true purpose. That false front — an act put on to deceive — is exactly what a pretense is.

How Pretense Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

guise

guise: a deceptive outward appearance

charade

charade: a false display kept up for show

sham

sham: something fake passed off as genuine

Antonyms

candor

candor: frank, open honesty

sincerity

sincerity: genuineness of feeling or intent

How Strong Is It? — act → pretense → masquerade

act vs. pretense

act vs. pretense: Putting on an act can be as small as hiding a bad mood; a pretense is a false front built specifically to deceive someone.

masquerade vs. pretense

masquerade vs. pretense: A masquerade goes further — an entire false identity, worn head to toe for as long as the deception needs to last.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — pre-

Prefix — pre-: before, in front (Latin prae-)

Root — tense (from tendere)

Root — tense (from tendere): to stretch (Latin tendere, tensum)

Put it together

Put it together: Pretense comes from pre- (before, in front) + tendere (to stretch): literally something 'stretched out in front' — a false front held up before others to hide the truth behind it.

Use the root in a new word: extend

Use the root in a new word: extend: When you extend a deadline, you stretch it further into the future — the same tendere root at work.

Root Check

Word Choice

Neutral — watch the idiom and the unit-mate

The most common idiom is 'under false pretenses' — gaining something through deception. And keep pretense apart from its unit-mate pretext (also taught in this unit): a pretext is the fake REASON you give for doing something, while a pretense is the fake APPEARANCE or act you keep up.
